paragraphs.text: She doesn't escort the dead to the afterlife, but instead raises them to fight and die again.
"More than snow falls from the Boreal skies." —Arkin Egilsson, skycaptain
"With his dream of unification fulfilled, Darien became the last king of Kjeldor. Those who followed were known as the kings of New Argive." —*Kjeldor: Ice Civilization*
The Knights of Stromgald struck Darien's Roost from two sides. They would have caught Kjeldor in a pincer attack were it not for Darien's tacticians.
The gargoyles were taken from the walls of flooded Kjeldoran cities and brought upland to guard the outposts of New Argive.
"I listen to people. He sniffs the wind. And we both sense something big coming. Something very big."
King Darien's breath crystallized and fell to the frozen battlefield, but its command carried true to all soldiers of New Argive.
"The White Shield is not the burnished metal you lash to your forearm but the conviction that burns in your chest." —Lucilde Fiksdotter, leader of the Order of the White Shield
"Only in our vulnerability is there true power, and that power is life itself."
The aberrant magic of the Rimewind drew the unicorns back from the northern wastes to do battle once again.
"The scouts claim the cold has malice, and a mind. I begin to believe them. Impassable drifts seem to appear before us at every turn." —Aevar Borg, northern guide, journal entry
"Heidar has forced the sun into hiding, but it has not forgotten us."
Darien's call to Yavimaya would have fallen red to the snow had it not been for the agility of the aesthir.
"Honor your steed and it will carry you to great deeds—and bring you home to tell of them."
Terisiare has only two kinds of weather: cold and weird.
"Artifice sundered the world. It shall not again wreak such sorrow."
"Whether frozen or fertile, the land is our ally. It awaits the call to battle."
Adarkar's blank wastes make the mind wander—and stray thoughts are quickly caught and devoured.
"Nature? Fire? Bah! Both are chaotic and difficult to control. Ice is structured, latticed, light as a feather, massive as a glacier. In ice, there is power!" —Heidar, Rimewind master
The Rimewind wizards strove to perpetuate a magical winter. Their unnatural snows birthed unnatural beasts.
"Guard, fetch me a mallet." —Heidar, Rimewind master
"The umber stain of the Thaw will be bleached away. Once again the world will be sharp, white, perfect!"
Plague-induced dreams became real as they swirled above Krov, mingling with the magical residue of the World Spell.
"Do not call the Balduvians barbaric. Their magic is as potent as it is primal." —Zur the Enchanter
When the School of the Unseen fell, so many magical treasures lay abandoned that no amount of death could deter the stream of thieves and desperate scholars.
"The Thaw brings flooding, disease, and death. We will do all in our power to bring frigid peace back to the world."
"Find solace in the sun? Burning, blinding, laying secrets bare? No, solace is found under the blanket of cold."
With the spread of Rimewind's sorcerous winter, snow dwellers reclaimed their places atop the food chain.
"Concentration is key. Without it, a mage conjures nothing but a splitting headache." —Zur the Enchanter
"Thick hides and layered armor won't help when I freeze you from the inside out." —Heidar, Rimewind master
Rimewind necromancers caught travelers in mystical blizzards then trapped their spirits in the mist of their final frozen breaths.
"I hope it's true that every snowflake is unique, because I never want to see one like this again. Now clean up that body." —Thangbrand Gyrdsson, Kjeldoran patrol
"You pray to Freyalise, but she cannot hear your pleas. It is Tevesh Szat who will claim your soul."
"Starving an army that feeds on its enemies is a sound strategy." —Garza Zol, plague queen
"There it was, clawing the ice as it chittered and clicked its teeth. We fled in horror before it unearthed its grisly meal." —Aevar Borg, northern guide, journal entry
"Make sure those wretches feed only upon the plagued. The blood of the healthy is reserved for me alone." —Garza Zol, plague queen
The few surviving humans of Krov would have welcomed the return of winter and its sterilizing cold. They often peered northward, hoping that the snow's edge had reached their infested city-tomb.
Puppeteered by Heidar's icy hand, they were sacrificed to the Frost Marsh to raise Haakon's army.
The unfortunates so transformed hungered not for flesh, but for warmth.
"Tresserhorn is ours now. Dredge the lake and bring me all the bones you find. We'll build you a new army, the likes of which Terisiare has never seen." —Heidar, Rimewind master, to Haakon
"The White-Shielders think their code justifies their actions. In truth it only binds their hands."
Kjeldorans who fled battle were exiled to the wastes. Those who strayed near Tresserhorn were pressed into service in Haakon's army.
The World Spell thawed their icy graves, promising rest in soft, quiet earth at last. But Heidar called them to duty for a twisted cause.
"Let your heartbeat be the thunder in the valley. Let your swords be the lightning on the peaks." —Lothar Lovisason, Balduvian chieftain
"To a trained mind, the cold is but a momentary distraction."
The people of Terisiare had come to live on frozen fields as though on solid ground. Nothing reminded them of the difference more clearly than the rifts brought on by the Thaw.
Clambering up and over the powdery slope, the goblin chanced upon a small furry thing. There they regarded each other: the goblin and his new pair of earmuffs.
Rimerunners set off avalanches to immobilize foes as well as to create more challenging slopes.
Having charted their way up the difficult face, the two mountaineers had to contend with the mountain's decision to stand up.
As the Thaw met Terisiare, mountains shed their icy skins, crushing homes and hopes alike.
"They're not easily trained. Fortunately, they already know how to kill." —Lovisa Coldeyes, Balduvian chieftain
Ice exploded into steam in its wake, hissing like a thousand serpents hailing their blazing master.
"I lead my horde to the northwest. I won't return until the ice wizards fall and their fiendish contraptions are crushed!"
She turns ash into flame and burns enemies to ash.
When a snowdrift shows you its eyes, it's already too late.
Blood calls to blood.
Deep beneath the ice, beneath the soil and the rock, Dominaria's fire still burned hot.
"This close to Rimewind Keep, no avalanche is nature's doing." —Ukoten, centaur chieftain
Slicking the ice with its heated underside, the thermopod skates at great speed to overtake its prey.
Those who used reindeer as beasts of burden knew to avoid the centaurs, who raged at the enslavement of their spirit-kin.
Some creatures are bound to the cold by Rimewind magic. Others seek it out, adapted by two thousand years of the Ice. The Boreal, where Heidar's frigid sway is strongest, is home to both.
"I have been trapped in the lizard's lair for days. It seems to regard me as its child and will not let me leave." —Aevar Borg, northern guide, journal entry
The aurochs herd is content to graze—until the bull provides the dissenting urge to charge.
Its white webs glitter, mimicking the frost on the tree's branches.
"Our border lands fall under the grip of Heidar's second winter. Go forth and reclaim them for Yavimaya." —Kaysa, elder druid of the Juniper Order
The strider's long, loping gait is an adaptation that allows it to move quickly in deep snow.
"Weep not for me. I will rise with the spring's new growth."
The sun-hot glow radiated from the druids, leaving scattered metal in steaming pools as it passed.
The ohran viper is not cold-blooded. Its veins course with the same antigelid venom used to kill its prey.
"Step lightly and we might be able to use it as a bridge." —Ib Halfheart, goblin tactician
"It's odd to see the apes rip down trees to arm themselves in defense of their forests." —Taaveti of Kelsinko, elvish hunter
"If you call the wolves, ensure you have a worthy hunt, or you may become the hunted." —Taaveti of Kelsinko, elvish hunter
Its belly produces a boiling-hot fluid it can spit as a weapon or spin slowly enough to freeze into a defensive web.
"There are deep, deep places in this world that have long burned hot with little regard for the whitening of the earth's thin skin." —Sek'Kuar, Deathkeeper
"That such delicate creatures could become so powerful in the embrace of winter is yet more proof that I am right." —Heidar, Rimewind master
To protect the alliance between Kjeldor and Yavimaya, they trained in the ways of both.
Karplusan legend told of an orc so cruel that he burned his own followers in rage—yet so revered that they rose from their pyres to serve him.
When Freyalise spoke the World Spell, the tamanoa rose to bring a new morning to Terisiare.
Out of sight, into mind.
"Don't be so quick to reclaim the thawing lands. They might have acquired a taste for freedom." —Taaveti of Kelsinko, elvish hunter
Zur remained aloof from Terisiare's suffering, intent only on his own perfection.
The Phyrexian death machine awoke, its coldsteel heart imbuing it with sinister new power.
"Arcum is a babbling fool! Phyrexian technology is our greatest blessing. Take this delightful trinket for instance . . ." —Heidar, Rimewind master
It took the Rimewind cultists days to realize they had successfully activated the creature—it just wasn't interested in moving.
Its plow wasn't designed for snow, but to carve a path through shrieking armies.
The Phyrexian minds that constructed it did not live past its awakening.
"A realm once green now ruled by Frost, Where flesh and field both pay its cost. Those dearly loved, forever lost . . ." —*The Dynasty of Winter Kings*
"Who will stay the Tyrant's hand, As ice and woe both grip our land? The helpless feel his frozen brand." —*The Dynasty of Winter Kings*
"Now caged in Winter's bitter chill, Our people cry, their voices shrill— Eternal cold breaks down their will." —*The Dynasty of Winter Kings*
"Our noble land, enslaved by Rime, Is it our fate to freeze through time? If this be true, oh wicked crime." —*The Dynasty of Winter Kings*
"Our land oppressed by silent Cold, We weary wretches, young and old, Pray that Springtime loose his hold." —*The Dynasty of Winter Kings*
